title: auth handshake — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: First message of every AFB WebSocket connection, replacing the legacy `{type: "auth"}` / `{type: "auth_ok"}` / `{type: "auth_error"}`. Same convention as the other schema-first afbws channels: routed by `channel` (`auth`) then by a mandatory `schema` id, no `type` field. There is no `request_id`: the handshake is exactly one request and one answer. Negotiation caveat: `support` is learned only from auth.ok, i.e. AFTER the client has already chosen the form of its first message — so the frontend ALWAYS sends afbws.auth.request.v1, and the backend accepts BOTH the legacy `type: "auth"` and this schema, answering in the form of the request (legacy request -> legacy auth_ok/auth_error; schema request -> afbws.auth.ok.v1 / afbws.auth.error.v1). The backend still lists `afbws.auth.v1` in `support` so a client can tell that the backend understands the new form. Removal of the legacy form is a separate decision. See AFB/docs/API_REGISTRY.md.

request.title: afbws.auth.request.v1 — handshake request (client -> server, first message).
request.description: The session is taken from the `afb_session` cookie, or from `session_id` when the cookie is absent/invalid. `version` (frontend build) is logged for monitoring only — never parsed, compared or used to gate behaviour; all behaviour is gated on `support` alone. `demo: true` = demo login (guest profile, GetCourse skipped).

support.description: afbws capability ids the client supports (x-afbws-support-id values).

session_id.description: HTTP session id, used when the cookie is unavailable.

ok.title: afbws.auth.ok.v1 — successful handshake (server -> client).
ok.description: `support` — the backend's own declared afbws capability ids (not the intersection; the client computes it). `brokers` — known broker ids for the link connector-create form, sent unconditionally. `access` — effective access of this connection (tier / capabilities / limits / mode ...), see common.v1.json#/$defs/access; later changes arrive as afbws.access.state.v1 pushes.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name of the platform (e.g. `Europe/Moscow`).

error.title: afbws.auth.error.v1 — failed handshake (server -> client); the server closes the socket right after it.
error.description: `unauthorized` — no valid session (close code 4001); `session_invalid` — the session exists but its access profile could not be resolved (close code 4001); `invalid_request` — the first message is not a valid auth request (close code 4000).
